verdict: Meridian is structurally disciplined but underperforming due to hindsight-biased sleeve selection, excessive complexity, and untested alpha, requiring an immediate pivot to the simpler C1 core while enforcing strict pod governance.

findings.claim: Sleeve selection suffers from severe hindsight bias, causing live underperformance.
findings.evidence: 4a/4d: picks chosen on 2026-06-28 by 10-year backtest return included recent winners; honestly selected picks trailed SPY (+13.5%) with best Sharpe 0.49.
findings.recommendation: Replace hindsight selection with out-of-sample walk-forward validation before deploying any new sleeve.

findings.claim: Overcomplication dilutes returns and leaves capital idle.
findings.evidence: 2/3: 8 sleeves, ~60% invested, equity flat $10,000 to $9,997 over 3 months while SPY +5.8% and same instruments +9.7%.
findings.recommendation: Execute the planned C1 switch immediately to consolidate capital and reduce transaction friction.

findings.claim: SVXY sleeve violates the fund's maximum drawdown mandate.
findings.evidence: 2/4c: SVXY max DD −37.7% vs mandate −15%; Sharpe 0.52.
findings.recommendation: Retire the SVXY sleeve on switch day as planned; volatility exposure is incompatible with the −15% risk budget.

findings.claim: Core exposure scaling relies on in-sample fitting, risking overconfidence.
findings.evidence: 6/7: CORE_EXPOSURE 0.78 fitted on the same 2008–2026 history it is judged on; unscaled drawdown −19%.
findings.recommendation: Reduce initial exposure to 0.70 and require out-of-sample live validation before scaling to 0.78.

findings.claim: DAY orders filling at the next open introduce gap risk and stale pricing.
findings.evidence: 2: Market DAY orders fill at the next open; slippage averaged −3.9 bps.
findings.recommendation: Switch to next-day limit orders or use after-hours execution to capture decision-time prices and reduce gap risk.

findings.claim: Paper account lacks dividend/coupon income, distorting C1 performance measurement.
findings.evidence: 3/7: Paper pays no income; C1 is ~78% bonds, dividend ETFs, and T-bills.
findings.recommendation: Deploy the total-return tracker immediately and adjust paper equity to reflect accrued income for fair evaluation.

findings.claim: Alpha pod beta hedging remains undefined, risking unintended market exposure.
findings.evidence: 1: Still open whether pods hedge their beta; multi-manager beta to S&P is ~0.03.
findings.recommendation: Mandate an explicit beta hedge (e.g., SPY short or inverse ETF) for all funded alpha pods to preserve market neutrality.

findings.claim: Timing signals consistently fail to beat simple buy-and-hold.
findings.evidence: 4c: sector_rotation, momentum, and trend timing show negative CAGR differences vs holding across all periods.
findings.recommendation: Deprecate timing signals that cannot survive costs; shift research focus to structural allocation and risk budgeting.

decisions.why: Aligns with owner risk tolerance and enables clean, enforceable pod stop-loss rules.
Evidence shows they trail SPY and add operational noise without generating alpha.

decisions.decision: Pod rules (−5% halve, −7.5% shadow, 12mo/30 trades shadow, ramp, ≤30% risk)
decisions.why: Matches institutional multi-manager standards and enforces strict capital discipline.
Simplifies structure, reduces friction, and matches honest baseline performance within risk limits.
In-sample fitting creates overconfidence; exposure must be conservatively sized pending live validation.

missed_risks: Broker liquidity and slippage during high volatility when DAY orders fill at the next open.
Paper trading masks real execution costs, bid-ask spreads, and market impact.
Concentration risk in C1 if SPY/IEF correlation spikes during a liquidity crisis.
Regulatory and tax implications of frequent ETF rebalancing if migrated to a taxable real account.

next_month.action: Execute C1 core switch and retire momentum, sector, trend, and SVXY sleeves
Implement total-return income tracker for paper account
Define mandatory beta hedging rule for alpha pods
Reduce CORE_EXPOSURE to 0.70 pending live validation
Validate Faber shadow sleeve logs against hold-out data

questions_for_owner: What is the exact statistical and duration trigger to transition Faber from shadow to funded status?
How will you handle the transition of real capital to Meridian once the C1 core proves stable live?
Should alpha pods be required to hedge beta, and if so, what instrument and sizing rule will you mandate?
How will you adjust the −15% max DD target if the core requires leverage to meet return expectations?
